items.q: An app identifies users with cookies in the same way a website does.
items.why: Apps mostly use mobile advertising IDs, such as the IDFA on iOS and the GAID on Android.

items.q: In-app ads are usually requested through an SDK that the app includes.
items.why: The ad SDK is code from an ad platform that requests and shows ads inside the app.

items.q: A rewarded video gives the user something in return for watching.
items.why: Users choose to watch and get a reward, such as an extra life or a bonus.

items.q: app-ads.txt does for apps what ads.txt does for websites.
items.why: The developer lists authorised sellers on their website so buyers can check who may sell the app inventory.

items.q: Mediation lets an app request ads from several ad networks and choose among them.
items.why: A mediation layer calls many demand sources and picks the best result for each slot.

items.q: Interstitial ads work best when shown in the middle of a task.
items.why: They work best at natural breaks, such as between levels, so they do not interrupt the user.

items.q: On iOS, apps must ask permission before tracking users across other companies’ apps and sites.
items.why: App Tracking Transparency asks the user, and without a yes the IDFA is not shared.
